newsitem.title: UK: Palladium group say no default has occurred.
newsitem.headline: Palladium group say no default has occurred.

text.p: No default has occurred in the platinum and palladium markets, the chairman of the London Platinum and Pallidium Market association said following a meeting of market makers.
"The members confirmed that there were no defaults in the market," said chairman Trevor Pitts, denying rumours of the past two days of a default.

The meeting was called on Thursday afternoon and involved the 10 full members of the London Platinum and Palladium Market plus the three Zurich-based clearing members, Pitts said. The Zurich members participated through a conference telephone call.
"We called the meeting in response to concerns about the tightness in the market and the idea was to exchange views on that position and to acknowledge those concerns," he said.
Members agreed that forward rates, which most of them stopped quoting due to the market tightness, would be done only on a "quote suggestion" basis for the time being.
"The members agreed to try to offer clients an orderly market in platinum and palladium. The key issue really depends on when the Russians begin exporting again," Pitts said.
The one-month lease rates for palladium reached over 300 percent on Wednesday reflecting the lack of available material to the market as the main supplier, Russia, has not exported since December.
